title: The Diophantine equation $p^{x}+6^{y}=z^{2n}$: a complete solution for half of the primes
summary: Let $p$ be a prime number and let $n\geq 1$ be an integer. We completely solve the exponential Diophantine equation $p^{x}+6^{y}=z^{2n}$ in positive integers $x,y,z$ for every prime $p$ such that the Legendre symbol $\leg{6}{p}$ equals $-1$, that is, for $p\equiv 7,11,13,17\pmod{24}$: the equation has no solution, with the single exception $(p,n,x,y,z)=(13,1,1,2,7)$. Since these residue classes contain half of all primes in the sense of Dirichlet density, this settles the equation for one prime out of two, uniformly in the exponent $n$. Two ingredients of the proof have independent interest.…
